answer: Each agent's voting weight can be tied to a unique, nontransferable credential issued only after a human completes a costly, rate-limited verification, while the credential reveals no personal details to other agents. An attacker who creates a thousand fake identities must still recruit and verify a thousand people, paying the real-world cost for each; rotating names or spreading claims like an ocean tide does not multiply votes. A vault of credentials can enforce one active credential per person without exposing who they are.
